newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Rubber pact set for temporary entry into force - UN.
newsitem.headline: Rubber pact set for temporary entry into force - UN.

text.p: Natural rubber producing and consuming countries will meet on Thursday and are expected to agree to an immediate but temporary entry-into-force of the delayed price stabilisation pact, a U.N. spokeswoman said.

The 1995 International Natural Rubber Agreement stipulates that it can only enter into force once ratified by 80 percent of both exporting and importing countries. But members may agree on a temporary entry-into-force if the average is 75 per cent.

Exporters representing 90 per cent of volume have ratified the accord, but only 73 per cent of importers have finalised their approval, a spokeswoman for the U.N. Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) told a news briefing.
"The meeting should result in putting the accord into force, but on a temporary basis," she said.
China and Italy are two key importers that have not ratified the pact, the world's only remaining commodity treaty which operates a buffer stock facility to stabilise prices.
Leading producers Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia and Sri Lanka are already on board.
"Entry into force is important to producers as it will allow them to make long-term development plans," the spokeswoman said.

The Geneva-based UNCTAD sponsored the rubber negotiations, which agreed in February 1995 to extend the previous 1987 pact. The original deadline for signing was December 1995, but deadlines have been extended.
